title: Director, R&D Scalable Manufacturing & Automation
text:
**Job Description**
Nokia Network Infrastructure is seeking a Director of Scalable Manufacturing & Automation to help define and execute the R&D technology roadmap for scalable, high-precision optical manufacturing. This leader will partner with internal engineering and operations teams and with third-party equipment manufacturers to specify, develop, qualify, and deploy next-generation automation that enables safe, repeatable, zero-defect volume production.
 
 
The successful candidate combines deep manufacturing-domain expertise with systems thinking, supplier leadership, and disciplined industrialization. The role spans mechanization, automation development, precision optical assembly and test.
 
 
**How You Will Contribute And What You Will Learn**
Key Responsibilities
 
 

* Develop a scalable manufacturing strategy: Build a multi-year automation and equipment roadmap aligned with product roadmaps, capacity plans, cost, yield, quality, and time-to-volume objectives.
* Scale production technology: Translate product and process requirements into robust manufacturing concepts, line architectures, equipment specifications, acceptance criteria, and deployment plans.
* Lead equipment partnerships: Work directly with third-party equipment manufacturers and integrators to develop new capabilities where commercial solutions do not yet meet Nokia’s precision, throughput, traceability, or reliability needs.
* Advance optical assembly: Industrialize automated pick-and-place, adhesive dispense and cure, precision lens placement, active and passive alignment, optical coupling, inspection, and functional test.
* Embed zero-defect principles: Design quality at the source through automated detection, stop-and-alert logic, interlocks, error proofing, closed-loop process control, defect containment, and rapid root-cause correction.
* Integrate the digital factory: Ensure equipment supports data collection, recipe governance, material and unit traceability, analytics, equipment health monitoring, and connectivity with manufacturing execution and quality systems.
* Manage execution and investment: Develop business cases, capital plans, resource models, schedules, technical risk assessments, and executive-level progress reviews.

**Required Qualifications**
**KEY SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, industrial, controls, materials, optical engineering, or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
* Substantial progressive experience in advanced manufacturing, automation, equipment engineering, or process industrialization, including leadership at a senior manager, director, or equivalent level.
* Demonstrated success specifying, co-developing, qualifying, and deploying custom or highly configured production equipment with external equipment manufacturers and system integrators.
* Knowledge of zero-defect manufacturing, quality at the source, error proofing, automated inspection, process capability, statistical process control, design of experiments, measurement system analysis, root-cause analysis, and corrective action.
* Experience industrializing optical assembly processes such as high-accuracy pick-and-place, lens placement, active or passive alignment, bonding, optical test, and automated inspection.
* Working knowledge of precision motion systems, machine vision, robotics, controls, fixtures, metrology, software and equipment interfaces, and manufacturing data systems.
* Strong commercial judgment in technical negotiation, capital justification, contract deliverables, and supplier performance management.
* Ability to work across R&D, product engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, IT/OT, facilities, and external partners in a global matrix organization.
* Clear executive communication, structured problem-solving, and change-leadership skills.
* Ability to travel to Nokia sites, supplier facilities, and equipment acceptance events as business needs require.

**Preferred Experience**

* Manufacturing of photonic integrated circuits, optoelectronic modules, coherent optical components, lasers, detectors, or high-density optical assemblies.
* Cleanroom manufacturing and materials or contamination controls relevant to photonics and semiconductor assembly.
* Factory automation architectures, machine connectivity, manufacturing execution systems, equipment data acquisition, advanced analytics, digital twins, or predictive maintenance.
* Global equipment transfer, replication across factories, contract manufacturing, or development of standardized manufacturing platforms.
* Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or equivalent operational-excellence certification.

**Measures of Success**

* Scalable manufacturing roadmap approved and translated into funded, executable programs.
* New equipment and processes achieve defined safety, quality, capability, throughput, availability, and cost targets at production release.
* Yield improves and defect escapes, manual interventions, rework, and unplanned downtime decline.
* Critical processes include effective built-in quality, traceability, automated detection, and relevant responses.
* Equipment suppliers meet technical, schedule, documentation, service, and lifecycle-support commitments.
* New products and processes transition smoothly from development to repeatable scale production.
